collection.description: Everyone else says it with a wink.

ask.text:
Once in a long while the moon rises red over the sea, and the old midwives say any child conceived under a red moon comes into the world in company. (midwife), the oldest healer, says it with a straight face. Everyone else says it with a wink.
Tonight the moon is red. (subject) and (friend) are sitting on the beach watching it come up, and (midwife) walks past them with (subject.his/her) lantern, stops, and says, very seriously, "I'd go inside, if I were you two. Unless you want to be busy."
Do (subject) and (friend) laugh it off and stay to watch the moon, or take the old healer's advice?

choices.label: Take the Advice and Go In

c1o1.text: A few weeks later (subject) is pregnant, and some weeks after that (midwife) presses an ear to her belly, listens for a long time, and holds up {#babies:one finger|two fingers|three fingers}. (friend) has to sit down. "It's only a story," (friend) says weakly, to anyone who will listen. (midwife) just smiles and starts weaving {#babies:a sleeping basket|a second sleeping basket|two more sleeping baskets}.

c1o2.text: In time (subject) is pregnant, with one baby, just one. (midwife) seems almost disappointed. "Well," (subject.he/she) says, "the moon can't be right every time." (subject) and (friend) decide that's the best kind of story: the kind that doesn't come true.

c1.text: They laugh, and (midwife) shrugs and walks on. The red moon climbs higher and the sea turns the colour of embers...

c2o1.text: On the healers' doorstep sits a basket with a baby in it, wrapped in a red cloth. Nobody in the village is missing one. (midwife) comes back, looks at the baby, looks at the moon, and looks at (subject). "Well," (subject.he/she) says. "Company, I said." (subject) and (friend) take the baby home that night.

c2o2.text: They go inside and sleep soundly. In the morning (midwife) asks how they slept, with a suspicious look, and they say "very well, thank you," and (subject.he/she) seems satisfied. Three huts over, the neighbours who stayed on the beach are very quiet at breakfast.

c2.text: (friend) laughs, but (subject) gets up. "Better safe," she says. They head back up the path, past the healers' hut, where a small sound is coming from the doorstep...
